2026-09-03T04:33:12.3018958Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3019322Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3019643Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3020112Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3020509Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3020991Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3022536Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3024218Z >
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3109213Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3113039Z >
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3113896Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3115274Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3115469Z ### How to Use
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3115710Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3117477Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3119791Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3120002Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3120684Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3121429Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3122676Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3122889Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3123166Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3123715Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3125015Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3125829Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3126878Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3128173Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3128386Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3129060Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3130308Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3130878Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3131561Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3132412Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3133024Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3133652Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3134196Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3135496Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3137163Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3137602Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3137875Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3138608Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3140030Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3141611Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3141794Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3142248Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3143091Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3143909Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3144430Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3144929Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3146544Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3147368Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3147846Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3148056Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3148778Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3149656Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3149837Z ```bash
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3150526Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3151397Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3152101Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3152536Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3152927Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3154254Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3154824Z ```
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3155033Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3155253Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3156075Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3157211Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3158204Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3159194Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3160321Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3160838Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3161024Z ### Notes
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3161245Z 
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3161851Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3163227Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3165251Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3166656Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3167835Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3168958Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3169907Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3170616Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-03T04:33:12.3171468Z <github-context>
